findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the allowlist truly requires an external data file, or whether an inline Python constant (matching the EXCLUDED_PREFIXES/BASE_ALLOWLIST/EXCLUDED_JOBS pattern used by every sibling check_*.py guard) is sufficient — the plan's 'reviewable as a diff' rationale applies equally to either.
evidence: scripts/check_dco_identity.py lines 26-31: `EXCLUDED_PREFIXES = ("infra/", ".github/workflows/", "tests/", "docs/experiments/")` — inline tuple, no external file
scripts/check_build_env_locked.py line 33: `BASE_ALLOWLIST = {"pip", "setuptools", "wheel"}` — inline set constant, no external file
scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py lines 63-72: `EXCLUDED_JOBS = frozenset({"external", "eval-live"})` — inline frozenset with per-entry justifications, no external file

Plan Scope section already fully enumerates all allowlist entries (~15 static paths/patterns): Jira fixtures, docs/archive/, docs/experiments/, 3 historical-citation sites, 4 O-RAN-SC sites, editor.js, 4 permanent vocabulary carve-outs, 2 test files — a bounded, fixed set
Plan rationale 'reviewable as a diff' is equally satisfied by a changed inline constant appearing in the script's own diff
findings.finding: The plan proposes 'The allowlist is a data file, not inline regex' — but every existing sibling guard script in scripts/ uses inline Python constants for bounded, static exemption sets (check_dco_identity.py: EXCLUDED_PREFIXES tuple; check_build_env_locked.py: BASE_ALLOWLIST set; check_verify_gate_parity.py: EXCLUDED_JOBS frozenset). The plan's stated rationale ('reviewable as a diff') applies equally to an inline constant. Introducing an external data file creates a new config-surface pattern not present in any sibling guard, adds a second artifact to locate and maintain, and provides no capability that an inline constant cannot for this bounded (~15-entry) static set.
findings.location: Approach section — 'The allowlist is a data file, not inline regex, so an exemption is reviewable as a diff.'
scenarios: An implementer adds an external JSON/YAML allowlist file, creating a new config-surface entry-point that all future contributors must locate separately from the guard logic.
Tests referencing the guard must also know the allowlist file path/format, adding indirection not present in sibling guard tests.
The data file's format (JSON? YAML? plain text?) is unspecified in the plan, leaving implementers to invent a convention with no precedent.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'The allowlist is a data file, not inline regex' with 'The allowlist is an inline Python constant in the guard script (e.g. EXCLUDED_PATHS tuple with per-entry comments), matching the EXCLUDED_PREFIXES/BASE_ALLOWLIST/EXCLUDED_JOBS pattern used by sibling check_*.py guards.' This satisfies the 'reviewable as a diff' property without introducing a new config-surface artifact.
